Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA), student questionnaireAbout · Using this site

About this site

This site describes the Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA), student questionnaire, published by Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD). It is generated from the repository pdt-pisa, which holds metadata built from the publisher's documentation: each variable's label, question text, codes and missing codes, and availability, with corrections and links between releases. Each fact says where it came from.

What it isn't

  • It isn't the publisher's site, and the publisher hasn't reviewed it. The publisher's own page for the dataset is https://webfs.oecd.org/pisa2022/index.html. Where this site and the publisher's documentation differ, the publisher's documentation is the source; the differences this repository knows of are listed as corrections.
  • It doesn't hold the data. The data come from the publisher, or from this repository's data release when the terms allow; see Getting the data.
  • It makes no analysis decisions: which answers count as agreement, which weights or cases to use, or how to recode. Those belong to the projects that use the data.

What they say
OECD Terms and Conditions: data may be extracted, downloaded, copied, adapted, printed, distributed, shared and embedded for any purpose, even commercial, with credit to the OECD using the dataset's citation. Written content published since 1 July 2024 is CC BY 4.0; earlier written content may be used, copied, distributed and adapted with citation, but commercial translation needs authorisation. Allen Downey decided on 2026-11-19 that data, documentation and metadata ship and that LLM processing is allowed, with an OECD credit as the notice.

PublicDataToolkit

The library and the standard that build this site: https://github.com/AllenDowney/PublicDataToolkit. This site was generated by version 0.2.2.

Reporting an error

  • In the publisher's documentation (a wrong label, a missing code, question text that belongs to another item): open an issue at https://github.com/AllenDowney/pdt-pisa/issues, with where you found it. This repository records such errors as corrections, with the evidence, and keeps the publisher's original; it also says whether the error was reported to the publisher.
  • In this repository's records (a wrong link, a code classified wrongly, a variable left out): open an issue at https://github.com/AllenDowney/pdt-pisa/issues.
  • To the publisher: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD).
